subject: Follow-up: dataflow & DPA clarifications (controller vs processor, subprocessors, breach notice)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@healthsync.com>, Sam Green <sam.green@medsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + DPA / residency materials from today's demo

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. I promised a short wrap-up with the items we discussed and the docs attached.

Recap (short):
- Dataflow: customer PII (patient identifiers + intake forms) will be sent to Redwood via API; HealthSync will control input routing and decide retention.
- Residency: you asked whether we can guarantee EU-only processing for EU patients — we have a VPC private deployment option and can pin region; I flagged this as something we should validate with Legal for the final DPA language.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor list (see Subprocessor_List_2027.csv).
- Breach notice: we typically commit to notifying customers within 72 hours for incidents where Redwood is the surface for the incident; specific wording and escalation criteria live in the DPA.

Attachments: DPA_v1.2.pdf (playing copy), Subprocessor_List_2027.csv, SOC2_Type2_redwood.pdf (redacted report stub).

Open items for you:
1) Can you confirm whether HealthSync will be the Controller for the use-case (i.e., you decide lawful basis for processing) or whether you'd prefer Redwood to be Processor? We can support both but the DPA language differs.
2) Residency requirement: is EU-only processing a hard requirement for the pilot or just a preference?
3) Retention for logs/PII: what are your minimum retention needs for request logs / traceability? We can recommend a default but want to align.

Next steps I suggest:
- You review the attached DPA and mark any redlines; if you want, we can do a short legal touchpoint next week.
- If EU-only is required for the pilot, we schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead to review deployment options.

Would love a quick reply with answers to items 1–3. If easier, I'm happy to schedule a 30-min call.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + DPA / residency materials from today's demo

Thanks Aditya — helpful summary and appreciates the materials. A few clarifying questions from our side after reviewing the DPA and subprocessor list:

- Controller/Processor: HealthSync will be the Controller — we set patient data policies. We need the DPA to reflect a processor role for Redwood. Please confirm the specific obligations we should expect under that mapping (e.g., assistance with DSARs, records of processing activities).

- Subprocessors: two quick asks — can you confirm whether any subprocessors process data in the EU currently (we're specifically asking about the vector search provider listed)? If not, are there EU-located alternatives or the ability to keep that subprocessor off the EU processing path?

- Breach notice timing: we need clarity on the escalation thresholds. Our internal policy requires that vendors notify us as soon as they become aware of an incident that may materially affect our data, and operationally we must have a written notice within 48 hours for incidents impacting patient PII. The DPA currently references 72 hours. Can you confirm whether 48 hours is possible? If not, we need to understand the eventual triage and what triggers an immediate notification vs later updates.

- Retention: For pilot/POC we need request logs and KV cache keys retained for 90 days to support audits. Is that feasible in hosted mode or would that require Dedicated/Private?

We're aiming to finalize the DPA and start the pilot in July; can you get back to us on the above by Monday so we can prepare legal review? Happy to hop on a call if needed.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of Compliance, HealthSync
alicia.torres@healthsync.com

Thanks — quick read and proposals below. High level: we can probably meet most asks but Legal will need a clean redline and Solutions/Infra will need a short tech note for the customer.

Breach notice timing:
- Proposal: commit to "initial written notification within 48 hours of Redwood's determination that a security incident has or is reasonably likely to have materially impacted Customer PII," with an understanding that initial notification may be limited in detail; follow-up updates will be provided on a defined cadence (24/72 hour updates) until resolution.
- Risk note: Legal should confirm whether the "reasonably likely" language is acceptable; we avoid admitting causation in the initial notice.

Subprocessor / residency:
- Infra note (prelim): in hosted mode our routing can prefer EU nodes but currently the vector vendor processes across regions for scale. We can implement an exclusion for EU processing for an individual tenant, but that requires a short ops configuration and acceptance testing (2-3 weeks). Dedicated/Private removes the need for vendor exclusions since all processing happens in the customer's VPC/region.
- Proposal: offer a scoped EU-only routing addendum for the pilot (ops configuration + validation). If the customer wants a contractual guarantee of EU-only processing for all time, push to Dedicated/Private.

Retention / logs:
- We can retain request logs and KV metadata for 90 days in hosted for the pilot. There will be a small storage/ingress cost; Solutions should provide a rough estimate for the monthly delta.

Next steps I'm planning:
1) I'll draft redline language for the breach notice and the subprocessor routing clause (deliverable: redline PDF) — target: EOD Monday.
2) Marissa, please confirm the ops steps and ETA for enabling the EU exclusion (2–3 weeks validation).
3) Aditya, propose a 30-min call with Alicia & Sam + Legal (Andrew) and Solutions (Infra lead) for Tuesday or Wednesday next week.

If you want, I can include a short one-page tech note for the customer describing the difference between hosted EU-routing and Dedicated deployment.

-ben
